claim: A gain byte over this type's low shelf does not build the shelf at the gain it names either, and it does not reach it the way the two mid sections of the same type are reached. One shelf is stored at the bottom of the printed range -- the full cut -- and the byte blends the dry path towards that, with a boost being the same section with its numerator and its denominator exchanged. In coefficients it is the same three multiply-accumulates the mid sections use, moved from the numerator to the denominator, and the two are not the same curve: the mid reading has the low shelf falling away half an octave sooner in the middle of the window than the unit does, and this one is out by a quarter of a band.
why_not_named: Which end of the range a part stores a section at is not visible from outside it any more than whether it blends at run time or holds a row per setting. What is claimed is the curve, and the two things about the part that produce it -- one stored section rather than one per gain, and a far side that costs no second section -- together with which end the stored one sits at, which is what this record separates and what the mid sections answer the other way.

measurements.why: The only record in the archive of a shelf gain asked anywhere but at the ends of its window: every setting between them and four steps past each. The floor is cited with the profiles because it is what decides which settings the reading places.

The high shelf's own gain, and it separates nothing: three settings, two of them the window's ends, which is the one place all four readings are the same section. Scored for its residual and cited for what it cannot say, because the claim is about the low shelf and this is why.

document_rows.read_as: Evidence that a page prints a range of twelve decibels each way against those two addresses. What the claim takes from it is where the stored section sits -- one end of that range, and this record says which end.

era_priors.claim: Blending one stored section against the dry path costs the same whichever end of the range the stored one sits at.
era_priors.why: Mixing a section's transfer towards unity in the numerator leaves its denominator alone; mixing it in the denominator leaves its numerator alone. Three multiply-accumulates between two stored rows either way, and a part has no reason of cost to prefer one. So which end it stores is decided by something else, and is worth reading off a unit rather than assumed.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: One of the two spellings needed a coefficient the other did not, which would make this a cost argument and not a measurement.

era_priors.claim: A first order shelf's cut is its boost turned over.
era_priors.why: A one-pole one-zero shelf at a gain and at its negative are the same pole and zero exchanged, so a part that has either has the other for one coefficient swap -- the same swap the peaking section uses, and the reason neither kind of section needs a second stored row for the far side of its byte.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: A cut of the same height as a boost came back a different shape, which is what the fourth reading in this class predicts and what the cut side of this record was read for.

adds: The record says what each setting of the low shelf's gain did to the band profile. This claim is the step from that to how the byte reaches the shelf, which no record says. What it adds over the claim beside it is that the answer the mid sections gave does not carry: the same four readings, the same type, the same run, and the shelves come back on the other side. Every model in this archive builds its shelves at the gain, which is the third of the four.

alternatives.reading: The shelf is stored at the top of the printed range and the dry path is blended towards it, which is what the two mid sections of this same type do.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It is wrong at every setting the reading places -- 16 of 16 -- and it is wrong the other way from all the others: it has the shelf falling away 0.601 octaves sooner than the unit on average, which is seven bands against the one this reading resolves. It is also the worst residual of the four. That the winner on the mid sections is the last of four here is the finding and not an inconsistency: the two are mirror images of each other and this record tells them apart.

alternatives.reading: The shelf is the one-pole section computed at the gain the byte names, or read out of a row stored per setting, which is the same curve.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It says the shelf falls away at nearly the same distance at every setting, because a one-pole shelf's pole and zero part by the gain and the shape between them barely changes. The unit's figure moves half an octave across the window and this reading's moves a tenth: 13 of 16 settings wrong, out by 0.332 octaves on average.

alternatives.reading: The same blend with a second section stored at the other end of the range for the other side of the byte, rather than one section turned over.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It is the winner on the cut side and cannot be told from it there, because a blend towards a stored cut is exactly what this claim says the cut is. On the boost side it is the reading that was ruled out above: 7 of 16 settings wrong, all of them boosts. A shelf whose boost is its cut turned over is what the unit has, and it is what a coefficient swap gives for nothing.

alternatives.reading: The high shelf is reached the same way as the low one, so this is a fact about shelves rather than about this shelf.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: A high shelf was asked and it is reached the same way. Not the slot this alternative named -- it named the standalone type's, and what was run is a combination type's pair, which is the mechanism the reading proposed rather than the address it pointed at. On that type both shelves store the cut: the high shelf's transition moves outwards as the shelf shrinks, which is the reading this claim closed on, and it is 0 of 4 settings out of place against 4 for the opposite end and 4 for the section built at its gain. The reading that wanted one row shared between a type's two shelves needed the high one to move inwards. It does not. data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-bands/04-01-10-the-shelves-a-combination-type-does-not-print-a-corner-for-in-twelfths.json.

refuted_by: A shelf at half its gain falling away where the width of the stored full-scale boost would put it, or where the section built at that gain would. Or a boost whose shape is not its cut's, at more than the one band this reading resolves. Or the same reading on another type's shelf coming back the mid sections' way.

residual.unit: the median residual in decibels over the span the byte commands, meaned over the records that carry a feature
residual.why: Reported and not read. The four readings are within a thousandth of the span of each other over these records, because the settings that separate them are the ones whose profile is smallest and carry the least of a record's span. It moves the right way -- the winner is best of the four and the reading it displaces is worst -- and that ordering is over a range too narrow to decide anything. What decided it is where the shelf falls away, which is stated as a property.

gross.why: The median residual over the span the effect commands, taken as the worst of the records scored. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

qualitative.why: Properties the unit's readings have that the model's readings must have too. No arithmetic over a residual rescues a model that cuts where the unit boosts.

power.beaten_by: contradicting a property the winner satisfies
power.why: The runner-up in the catalogue, scored on the same records, and whether it leans or contradicts a property where the winner does neither. The decoy is not chosen -- it is whichever candidate came second, so a strawman cannot be put up in its place. A class holding one candidate is a catalogue that is unfinished, which is a finding and not a pass.

breakdown.why: A point worse than 0.5 of the span is a failure at that point rather than error at it. A residual that leans with the setting or with frequency is pointing at a structure the model does not have; one that does not is pointing at the room and the converters, and is not made smaller by anything this project can do.

where_the_shelf_has_fallen_by_half.what: The octaves from a band inside the shelf's own plateau to where the deviation has fallen to half of what it is at that band, at each setting one to eleven steps from the centre of the window. Read off the unit's profile and off each rendering by one reading, so whatever the band set does to a shelf it does to all five.
where_the_shelf_has_fallen_by_half.anchored_and_not_from_the_plateau: Because the plateau is not in the band set at every setting. At the top of the window this shelf is still climbing at the bottom band, so a figure taken as a fraction of a plateau would be a fraction of a number the run holds at one setting and not at another -- a bias that is a property of the setting, which is the one kind a reading may not carry. An anchor band has none: both sides are read at the same band.
where_the_shelf_has_fallen_by_half.read_as: The unit's figure moves outwards as the shelf shrinks, from about one and a half octaves at eleven steps to about two at two steps, and it does it the same way on the boost and on the cut. The blend with the stored section at the cut end follows it at every one of the 16 settings the reading places, out by 0.023 octaves on average, which is a quarter of a band. The section built at the gain hardly moves at all. The blend the mid sections use moves the other way.

what_the_placement_rule_decides.what: The figure is an interpolation between the two bands the half point falls between, so what places it is the step the profile takes across them. Where that step is under the run's own floor there the reading returns nothing, because an interpolation across a step smaller than the floor is an interpolation of the floor. Decided on the unit's profile alone: handing a candidate the same guard would let one escape a setting by being flat in it.
what_the_placement_rule_decides.read_as: It decides the verdict and it does not decide the winner. Without the rule the ranking is the same, in the same order, and the winner is wrong at one setting of twenty-two -- which is a shelf of one decibel at the anchor, where the unit's own reading at that setting and at its mirror are further apart than the tolerance the comparison asks of a model. With the rule that setting is not read and the winner is wrong at none, which is the difference between `rejected` and `reproduces`. Both figures are here because the second of them is the one the verdict rests on.

what_the_high_shelf_showed.what: Three settings, two of them the window's ends. All four readings are the one section at an end of the window, so nothing here separates them and nothing is claimed from it.
what_the_high_shelf_showed.read_as: The winner's worst point on the two high shelf records is about half the other three readings', and that figure is reported and not leaned on. At the window's end the four differ only in which gain the section was prewarped at when it was bilinear transformed, and where a part prewarps is a choice this archive made in its own renderer rather than one it has measured. No gate turns on it: every candidate passes breakdown on these records either way.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Why the shelves and the mid sections store opposite ends.
what_this_does_not_close.why: Nothing measured here says. The cost is the same either way, so the reason is something the part has that a band profile does not show -- a row shared with another section, a sign convention in a table, or nothing at all.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would: Not a measurement of this unit. The nearest thing to evidence is the high shelf answering one way rather than the other, which is the standing alternative above and is five minutes of hardware.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Every other type that prints a gain against a shelf.
what_this_does_not_close.why: One shelf of one type is read. The gain window and its clamp were folded onto other types and hold there, but those runs asked the window's ends, which is where every reading in this class agrees.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would: Four settings in the middle of the window on one of them, under the hold this archive has used twice.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Whether the shelf is one pole or two. This claim is scored on the one-pole shelf the type's own claim closed on.
what_this_does_not_close.why: The order was settled against the full-gain records and is not re-asked here. What this reading separates is the path, and it separates it by a quarter of an octave against candidates an octave apart -- so a second-order shelf reached the winner's way would still be the winner's way.

what_it_would_change: A renderer of this line building its shelves at the gain asked for is right at the ends of the byte and puts the shelf's own transition half an octave out in between, which is most of what a shelf at a modest setting sounds like. A renderer that took the mid sections' answer and carried it across to the shelves -- the obvious thing to do with the claim beside this one -- would be wrong by twice that, and in the other direction.
a_note_on_the_two_halves_of_this_class: The mid sections and the shelves of one type were put to the same four readings on records from the same runs, and they answered oppositely: the peaks store the boost and the shelves store the cut. The first scoring of the shelves was done with the peaks' instrument -- the count of bands a feature stands over half its height in -- which on a shelf counts up from the bottom of the band set, and under it the shelves merely refused the blend without saying what stood instead. The reading that answered is a shelf's own, and the candidate it found was not in the class at the time: three readings were scored, all three were wrong, and the one that fits was written because the runner-up fitted one half of the byte and its mirror fitted the other.

read_on_another_types_pair_of_shelves.what: The two shelves of `04 01`, a combination type whose equaliser prints a low gain, a mid section and a high gain and prints no corner byte for either shelf. Thirty takes, eleven settings a byte: the two ends of the gain window, two settings past each of them, the centre, and three, six and nine steps either side. Read by importing the run that made the claims rather than by restating their numbers.
read_on_another_types_pair_of_shelves.why_the_candidates_are_scored_at_their_o: These shelves have no corner byte, so no candidate can be handed a corner off a table the way the standalone type's was. Each is given the corner that suits it best, scanned at the ends of the window where all four are the same section -- and then judged on the shape across the window, which one number cannot fix.

the_high_shelf.read_as: The unit's figure moves outwards as the shelf shrinks and does it the same way on the boost and on the cut, which is what this claim's low shelf does on another type. The winner follows it within half a band at every setting the reading places and is the best residual of the four. The other three are wrong at every one of them, by five to eleven bands, and two of them are wrong asymmetrically where the unit is symmetric.

the_low_shelf.what_it_answers: The window and the corner, and not the path. Its corner lands near the bottom of the band set, so the shelf's plateau is under the lowest band this stimulus reaches and there is nothing to anchor the reading on: every candidate is out of place, including the one the high shelf settles on. That was stated before the scoring and not found in it.
the_low_shelf.what_would_answer_it: A stimulus with something below thirty hertz in it, which is not this archive's held note, or a band set that does not end at twenty-five. Neither is a run: it is a different reading of a take that does not carry the frequencies.

where_the_shelves_hinge.what: A figure no page prints and no record here held. Scanned over a grid at the ends of the gain window, and calibrated first on a shelf whose corner is already published: on the standalone type's low shelf the same scan returns 214.3 Hz where the chain claim holds 217.1, which is 0.019 octaves.
where_the_shelves_hinge.and_it_is_the_first_state_of_the_printed: The standalone type gives its low shelf two states and the chain claim holds them at 118.0 and 217.1 Hz. This one is 0.06 octaves from the first of those, which is under one band of the set it was read on. So a combination type's low shelf is the standalone type's low shelf with its corner byte stuck at the lower state -- and not at the state the standalone type powers up holding, which is the other one.
where_the_shelves_hinge.and_it_matches_neither_state: The standalone type's high shelf states are held at 6727.2 and 10960.9 Hz. This one is 0.23 octaves above the first and 0.47 below the second, so it is neither -- but the comparison is not like for like, because those two figures come from a record that sweeps the corner byte and this one from a record that sweeps a gain. Put to the standalone type's own high shelf gain record, this scan wants a corner at the top of what a thirty-two kilohertz chain can hold, so the instrument cannot state that state at all.

and_the_window_held.what: The gain class's window and clamp on two bytes that had never been asked, read off the high shelf's plateau because the low shelf's is under the band set.
and_the_window_held.read_as: A decibel a step from 52 to 76 and clamped outside it, to a tenth of a decibel over eleven settings. 0 returns what 52 returns and 127 what 76 returns.
